 Xbox Loses Its First Chief Operating Officer After Several Months
 Written by Erren Van Duine 
 Published: October 23, 2026 6:28 PM
 Share: Facebook 
 X 
 Reddit 
 Email 
 More shakeups over at Xbox today as their first person to lead the newly-created chief operating officer position has stepped down. Helen Chiang, who has worked at Microsoft for over 21 years, stepped into the position in July and will now be leaving the company entirely. 
 According to a memo obtained by The Verge , Xbox CEO Asha Sharma shared news of the departure today. While wishing Chiang well, Sharma says that her immediate responsibilities will be split amongst other Xbox leaders for the time being, and that they'll share more on the COO position as they finalize their own plans.
 While there's no outward reason for Chiang's departure, it seems obvious the role will continue in some capacity at Xbox. The COO role was originally created as part of Sharma's big "Xbox reset" that's taken over the division in recent months.
 This is also coming at a time where Xbox is in the midst of further layoffs, including speculation that more will be carried out in November and January. Back in July, Microsoft planned to cut over 3,200 positions, with 1,600 out at that time, and a further 260 people in September.
 This apparent reset has also impacted Xbox's major studios including Double Fine, Compulsion Games, and Ninja Theory with the former too now independent whilst Ninja Theory is facing closure as it started laying off staff a couple of weeks ago without a buyer.
